- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–7 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–3% per day until closer to historical range.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 5–10% gap), reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next 2–5 days.
